name: swapy
title: Swapy Layout Primitives
description: A grid of rounded cards, each with a small six-dot grip in the corner. Dragging one lifts it out of its slot and greys the other slots as targets; dropping swaps the cards' places with a spring.
use: Users should be able to rearrange dashboard widgets or tiles into their own order.
avoid: The grid is demo CSS; the parts only enable dragging, so they set no layout and do not save the new order.
a11y: Reordering is pointer drag only: the grip is an unfocusable div with no role or name, so keyboard users cannot move cards. (keyboard: no, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A bento grid on black: a wide monochrome pier photo card across two columns, a dark Revenue tile beside it, then a dark Subscribers tile, a white Conversion tile and a blue cloud photo card. Every card is rounded, thinly bordered and carries a dotted grip at its top left.
behaves: Pressing a grip lifts the card off its slot, floats it over the grid and dims it while the other slots tint grey as drop targets. Releasing over a slot puts the card there, sends the card that was there into the vacated slot and settles the grid with a short spring.
customise: You wrap slots and items and give each an id plus className; the layout takes an id, a config for animation, swap mode and auto-scroll, and an onSwap callback.
weight: light: Five static cards and a drag handler that only runs while a card is held.
demo: Revenue $48.2k, Subscribers 3,912, Conversion 4.7%, a Summer campaign photo and a cloud photo.
issues: The lifted card floats over the slot it is aimed at, hiding the target underneath.
Cards can only be moved by pointer drag, with no keyboard path through the grips.
The swapped order lives only in the page state, so a reload resets the grid.
polishWhy: Crisp card grid and a convincing lift and swap; the floating card hides its target.
